audit.why: Even lane at 48.97% over 4433 games; LeBlanc holds levels 1-6, Viktor takes over at two items. Page chart and packet levelChart agree, so no chart rows moved.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text used the fabricated ultimate name 'Chaos Storm'.
audit.why: Riot's kit file names Viktor's R Arcane Storm (120/100/80s). Passive is Glorious Evolution, banking Hex Fragments on kills to augment abilities.
audit.corrected: All four spikes and the phase prose now say Arcane Storm; the late spike is grounded in the augment stacking rather than a made-up 'Hex Core evolve' timer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two decisive interactions were absent: Arcane Storm is a channel, and Siphon Power is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Viktor's R carries the channel flag ('interruptible — any CC cancels it'); Ethereal Chains (E, 14s at rank 1) and a Mimicked chain both cancel it. Siphon Power (Q, 9s at rank 1) carries autoReset, so the wind-up — not the cast — is the tell that his burst is starting.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now names Gravity Field's 17s/13s, Arcane Storm's 120s channel and that Ethereal Chains cancels it.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Death Ray' used for Viktor's E in early and whys[0]/wants.foe[1].
audit.why: Riot's name is Hextech Ray (E, 12/11/10/9/8s, 525 range, line projectile).

edits.before: Late LeBlanc picks: W the flank, chain the carry, mimic the exit — and vanish before the obituary prints.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. It governs your forward steps. - W Distortion (return) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Gravity Field (W): 17s at rank 1, 13s at rank 5 — the stun zone owns every all-in; step out or fight before he places it. - Arcane Storm (R) on 120s is a channel: your Ethereal Chains cancels it. - Distortion's return spent on poke is a death you scheduled.

edits.before: Q the sigil, W the detonation, return before the answer — a half-bar round trip he experienced as weather.
edits.after: At 6, Mimic a second Ethereal Chains or Distortion: chain, Q-sigil, mimic, and the half-bar becomes the whole bar.

edits.before: Viktor spends Gravity Field early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Plates and roams outrun Hex Fragments — every minute before he banks augments is worth more to you.

edits.before: Staying at the W landing spot for one more auto — the return timer is your champion; outliving it is optional.
edits.after: Farm quietly and Viktor banks Hex Fragments to evolve ability after ability — your knife dulls while his zone grows.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Viktor wins by dropping Gravity Field on your entry, chipping Hextech Ray, and evolving past your burst.

edits.before: Carry through picks — one chained carry per objective; your job is the flank angle and the discipline to leave after.
edits.after: Carry through picks — chain Viktor himself off his 120s Arcane Storm; without the storm his team owns no ground mid.

edits.after: Viktor has no dash or blink at levels 1-2, so your burst punishes him whenever Hextech Ray poke misses or Gravity Field isn't set

edits.before: Chaos Orb-Ethereal Chains threatens lethal before his Chaos Storm can zone you out, so if you catch him without Gravity Field up you win the direct fight.
edits.after: Sigil-Ethereal Chains threatens lethal, and the chain cancels Arcane Storm outright — catch him with Gravity Field on its 17s and you win the direct fight.

edits.before: Once Viktor's Hex Core is fully evolved and his Chaos Storm zones entire fights, his AoE damage and area denial start outscaling your single-target burst, flipping the matchup his way.
edits.after: Once Viktor has banked enough Hex Fragments to augment his kit and his Arcane Storm zones entire fights, his AoE and area denial outscale your single-target burst, flipping the matchup his way.

edits.before: You win the 1-2 trade because Viktor has no dash or blink and his Siphon Power only reduces incoming damage rather than escaping it — bait his Death Ray poke, then punish with E-Q before he can reposition. His early damage is low relative to his scaling, so most exchanges before level 3 favor your burst if you engage from an angle he can't punish with Gravity Field.
edits.after: You win the 1-2 trade because Viktor has no dash or blink and Siphon Power only shields damage rather than escaping it — bait his Hextech Ray poke, then punish with E-Q before he can reposition. His Q wind-up is an auto-attack reset, so the animation, not the cast, is your cue to step out of Gravity Field range before he commits.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay in your favor since Distortion lets you dash around his Gravity Field zone and burst him down before Chaos Storm becomes a threat — if you catch him without his ultimate or zone control ready, you kill him clean. Watch for his evolved Hex Core abilities adding slows or extra damage that make your engage riskier as he scales.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 stay in your favor since Distortion lets you dash around his Gravity Field zone and burst him before Arcane Storm matters — and if he does cast the storm, Ethereal Chains cancels the channel outright. Gravity Field is 17s at rank 1: the moment it drops, that window is yours to step into and kill him in.

edits.before: Viktor flips the matchup once his Hex Core is fully evolved and Chaos Storm zones out entire fights with sustained AoE damage — his area denial and safety net from Gravity Field start beating your single-target burst combo. Late-game you need picks and flanks through stealth rather than straight engages, since a head-on Chaos Storm trade now favors him.
edits.after: Viktor flips the matchup once his augments are banked and Arcane Storm zones out entire fights with sustained AoE damage — his area denial and the Gravity Field safety net start beating your single-target burst. Play flanks and picks rather than straight engages, and chain him the instant he starts the storm: the channel dies to your E.

edits.after: Augment Hextech Ray for its trailing explosion

notes: CHART: all seven full-layer sides read 'Skill' while packet.levelChart and content win[] both give LeBlanc stages 1-6 and Viktor two-items. No paired win[N] edits are proposable — the content layer already holds the correct values. Ratings untouched. Fixed all three lintFindings. 'Chaos Storm' and 'Hex Core' are legacy pre-rework names; Riot's kit file gives Arcane Storm (R) and the Glorious Evolution / Hex Fragment augment system, so both were replaced. Kit text for R is truncated mid-sentence in _kits/viktor.json ('whenever champions die after taking damage from it, the') — the augment's actual effect could not be sourced, so no claim was made about it.
